precepts.text: The previous chapter opens Behemoth, the beast set to rule the earth, before chapter 41 turns to Leviathan of the sea.
precepts.point: He asks whether you can draw out Leviathan with a hook or his tongue with a cord, or put a hook into his nose or bore his jaw with a thorn, comparing this massive creature to fishing for a small fish. Leviathan is a massive, massive creature.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

precepts.why:
The Most High is speaking about Leviathan, one of the beasts he created. He made two great beasts: Behemoth to rule the earth and Leviathan to rule the waters. The chapter before opens Behemoth: “Behold now behemoth, which I made with thee; he eateth grass as an ox.”

Then chapter 41 turns to Leviathan, the one that deals in the waters. “Canst thou draw out leviathan with an hook? or his tongue with a cord which thou lettest down?” He compares this massive creature to fishing for a small fish, putting a hook into his nose or boring his jaw through with a thorn. Leviathan is a massive, massive creature, made by the Most High just as Behemoth was.

points: He asks whether you can draw out Leviathan with a hook or his tongue with a cord, or put a hook into his nose or bore his jaw with a thorn, comparing this massive creature to fishing for a small fish. Leviathan is a massive, massive creature.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: The Most High asks whether Leviathan will make many supplications, speak soft words, make a covenant, or be taken for a servant forever. This beast is not something a man can tame, play with like a bird, or bind for his maidens.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: No one can fill his skin with barbed irons or his head with fish spears. Lay a hand upon him, remember the battle, and do no more, for the hope of taking him is in vain and a man is cast down even at the sight of him.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: None is so fierce that he dare stir Leviathan up. Then the Most High turns it: who can stand before Him, who has ever given to Him first that He should repay, for whatsoever is under the whole heaven is His.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: The Most High will not conceal Leviathan's parts, his power, nor his comely proportion. No one can uncover the face of his garment or come at him with a double bridle.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: His teeth are terrible round about, and his scales are his pride, shut up together as with a close seal. They are so near one to another that no air can come between them, joined and stuck together so they cannot be sundered. These are tight scales.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: By his sneezings a light shines, and his eyes are like the eyelids of the morning. Out of his mouth go burning lamps and sparks of fire leap out. Out of his nostrils goes smoke as out of a seething pot or cauldron, his breath kindles coals, and a flame goes out of his mouth.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: In his neck remains his strength, and sorrow is turned into joy before him. The flakes of his flesh are joined together, firm in themselves and unmovable, and his heart is as firm as a stone, as hard as a piece of the nether millstone.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: When Leviathan raises himself up, the mighty are afraid. This is a beast that would terrify the mightiest of men, and no man is going to come up and fight him, because the Most High made him to rule the sea, strong and great above all the creatures in his domain.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: The sword, the spear, the dart, and the habergeon cannot hold against him. He esteems iron as straw and brass as rotten wood, so weapons of iron and brass do nothing. The arrow cannot make him flee, sling stones turn into stubble, darts are counted as stubble, and he laughs at the shaking of a spear.

note.label: Job 41: Leviathan, the King Over All the Children of Pride

points: He makes the deep to boil like a pot and the sea like a pot of ointment, and makes a path to shine after him. Upon earth there is not his like, a creature made without fear, and he is a king over all the children of pride. It sounds so far-fetched that it is hard even to imagine, and the scriptures say the kingdom will be a place we cannot even imagine, so we cannot imagine what these beasts look like either.
